findings.description: Under sub-criterion 1.2 (soundness of methodology), the schedule freezes and registers the primary model and model card (D2.1) at month 3, yet the harmonised database/variable-availability map (D1.1) and the stress-target, feature-selection and validation protocol (D1.2) — the artifacts that define the physiological target and the leakage-safe validation design the model depends on — are only delivered at month 14. An evaluator will read the model being frozen eleven months before its own defining protocol and harmonised data base as an internal-plausibility gap that undermines the otherwise strong 'freeze-before-validation' argument.
findings.evidence: "the primary model is then developed and frozen, delivering D1.3 and D2.1 at month 3 ... delivering D1.1, D1.2 and D2.2 at month 14".
findings.recommendation: Reconcile the month-3 model freeze with the month-14 delivery of D1.1/D1.2 — either explain that a provisional target/protocol is fixed and documented pre-freeze (with D1.1/D1.2 as later formalisations) or adjust the stated due months so the defining protocol precedes the freeze.

findings.description: Under sub-criterion 1.1 (ambition and going beyond the state of the art), the proposal explicitly disclaims methodological/algorithmic novelty and locates its advance in a validation framework and parsimony. While defensible, a critical evaluator scoring the 50%-weighted Excellence criterion may judge the ambition 'beyond the state of the art' as modest, since the core deliverables are harmonisation, validation discipline and an MVP rather than a new scientific method.
findings.evidence: "The genuine novelty is not a new machine-learning algorithm ... but the construction and demonstration of a validation framework".
findings.recommendation: Sharpen the beyond-SotA claim by stating concretely what is not currently possible in the field and what new, citable scientific knowledge (not just process rigour) the validation framework produces, so ambition is anchored in a demonstrable advance.

findings.description: Under sub-criterion 1.3 (supervision, training and two-way transfer), the competence gap the fellowship exists to close — rigorous predictive modelling/ML and validation — is carried by the ELTE-side team member (Hollós) and the EO co-supervisor (Jung), both at an associated partner whose participation and the co-supervision acceptance are declared assumptions pending written confirmation. Placing the central training expertise outside the beneficiary host, on unconfirmed commitments, is a dependency risk for the action's core objective.
findings.evidence: "the predictive-modelling/machine-learning methodological leadership is carried by a named ELTE-side team member"; ELTE participation is "assumed ... awaiting ELTE written associated-partner confirmation".
findings.recommendation: Strengthen evidence that the modelling/EO training capacity is secured (e.g. flag imminent associated-partner and co-supervision letters) and clarify how the host guarantees continuity of the central training strand if the associated-partner arrangement changes.

findings.description: Under sub-criterion 1.4 (researcher's professional experience), the researcher's demonstrated output in the modelling and Earth-observation domain — precisely the domain at the scientific core of the action — is thin, resting on mobilities, a UAV licence and a small number of contributing-author remote-sensing papers rather than a substantive publication or modelling track record. An evaluator may view this as a shortcoming in the appropriateness of the demonstrated competences.
findings.evidence: "of her nine recorded publications only a small number touch remote sensing, all recent and as a contributing author".
findings.recommendation: Reinforce appropriateness by foregrounding any concrete modelling/EO outputs, datasets or tool artefacts (including DrR functionality already built) to evidence hands-on capability, while retaining the honest gap framing.

findings.description: Under sub-criterion 2.3 (magnitude and importance of the contribution), the proposal declines to state any project-specific quantified impact target for water saving, water productivity or economic value, relying instead only on bounded literature ranges (approx. 8–30%). While methodologically honest, the criterion explicitly scores magnitude; declining to commit to any measurable project-level impact figure weakens the demonstrable magnitude an evaluator can credit.
findings.evidence: "the project makes no fixed-percentage water-saving promise" / economic value "is deliberately not expressed as an invented EUR/ha or fixed water-saving figure".
findings.recommendation: Add conditional, method-anchored target ranges or expected-effect envelopes (e.g. detection lead-time and water-productivity improvement bounds the design is powered to demonstrate) so magnitude is quantified as a defensible expectation, not only as retrospective literature context.

findings.description: Under sub-criterion 2.3, the societal-magnitude case invokes EU-scale horticulture figures (approximately 2.0 million hectares, 0.7 million farms) as the potential application domain. The pathway from a single-crop, single-fellow action to that scale is asserted rather than substantiated, and an evaluator may see the scale claim as loosely connected to what the action itself can deliver.
findings.evidence: "Eurostat reports fresh vegetables cultivated over approximately 2.0 million hectares in the EU in 2023 ... presented explicitly as a potential application domain and not as an immediate addressable market".
findings.recommendation: Tighten the scale-to-action linkage by quantifying the near-term reachable segment (e.g. processing-tomato area in the target countries) alongside the broad domain figure, so magnitude is graduated from what the project touches to the wider potential.

findings.description: Under sub-criterion 2.1 (career perspectives and employability), the broad set of target employability destinations (universities, research organisations, precision-agriculture and irrigation firms, EO/geospatial organisations, FMIS providers) is asserted as a spread rather than evidenced through concrete post-fellowship prospects, contacts or a defined next-step trajectory. The credibility of the employability claim would be higher with a more concrete destination narrative.
findings.evidence: "explicitly relevant to universities, European research organisations, precision-agriculture and irrigation-technology companies, Earth-observation/geospatial organisations, crop-phenotyping groups and farm-management-information-system (FMIS) providers".
findings.recommendation: Anchor the employability breadth in one or two concrete post-fellowship trajectories (target roles/sectors and the transition mechanism) and reference the specific career KPI used to measure the outcome.

findings.description: Under sub-criterion 2.2 (dissemination, exploitation and communication), success is defined largely by output counts (two peer-reviewed papers, an optional third, one public demonstration and one public-facing article per year) without quantified audience-reach or uptake targets. Although proportionate to a single-researcher action, the absence of measurable reach/uptake indicators limits the evaluator's ability to judge the quality and effectiveness of the measures.
findings.evidence: "the project targets one public field demonstration with farmers and one public-facing article per year".
findings.recommendation: Add a small number of measurable dissemination/uptake indicators (target audiences reached, farmer participants, MVP evaluation users) tied to named channels, keeping them proportionate to a single fellow.

findings.criterion: Quality and efficiency of the implementation
findings.description: Under sub-criterion 3.1 (effort appropriateness and work-plan effectiveness), the single fellow must simultaneously execute WP1 (9.0 PM to month 14), the campaign-intensive WP3 field validation, and continuous WP4 co-development running month 1–24. The concurrency of three demanding strands on one researcher raises a workload-feasibility concern that the effort table (WP4 spread thinly across 24 months) does not fully dispel.
findings.evidence: "WP4 runs in parallel from month 1 to month 24" while WP1 (M1–14) and WP3 field campaigns proceed, executed by a single researcher at 30 PM total.
findings.recommendation: Demonstrate the concurrency is realistic by showing month-by-month effort loading at peak overlap, and clarify how partner in-kind support (Krumatic development, ELTE UAV operation) offloads the fellow during simultaneous WP1/WP3/WP4 activity.

findings.criterion: Quality and efficiency of the implementation
findings.description: Under sub-criteria 3.1/3.2, WP3 is designated as led by 'the independent commercial-farmer validation site', which the section itself states is a collaborating environment that is neither a beneficiary nor an associated partner and whose written field access is still to be secured. Assigning work-package leadership to an unnamed, non-partner site without a confirmed agreement is an accountability and capacity weakness for the validation work package.
findings.evidence: "WP3 ... (lead: the independent commercial-farmer validation site)" while that site is "a collaborating validation environment, not a beneficiary or associated partner".
findings.recommendation: Reassign scientific leadership of WP3 to the beneficiary/fellow (with the farmer site as a hosting/collaboration environment) so accountability rests with a formal participant, and reference the T3.1 access agreement and contingency ladder as the risk control.

findings.criterion: Quality and efficiency of the implementation
findings.description: Under sub-criterion 3.1 (work-plan clarity), the work-package set is numbered WP1, WP3, WP4, WP5 with no WP2 and no in-section explanation for the gap. An evaluator encountering a missing WP number without justification may find the structure confusing and question work-plan coherence.
findings.evidence: "The work plan is deliberately compact — four work packages ..." listed as WP1, WP3, WP4, WP5 (no WP2).
findings.recommendation: Either renumber the work packages consecutively (WP1–WP4) or add a one-line note explaining that the former WP2 was merged into WP1, so the numbering gap is not read as an omission.

findings.criterion: Quality and efficiency of the implementation
findings.description: Under sub-criterion 3.2 (quality and capacity of participating organisations), the two organisations central to the exploitation/operationalisation chain (AgroVIR, Krumatic) have no EU-funded research track record, AgroVIR holds no PIC yet, and the host's recent institutional transformation is flagged for Part A verification. Taken together these introduce capacity and legal-status uncertainties around the participants the impact pathway most depends on.
findings.evidence: "AgroVIR holds no PIC yet" and "declares no participation in EU-funded research projects".
findings.recommendation: Reinforce capacity by evidencing the commercial/operational competence that substitutes for a research track record and confirming registration/legal-status actions (PIC registration, host Part A verification) are in hand before submission.

revision_actions.action_description: Resolve the sequencing tension by stating that a provisional stress-target and validation protocol are fixed and documented before the month-3 freeze (with D1.1/D1.2 as their formalisation), or adjust the D1.1/D1.2 due months so the defining protocol and harmonised base precede D2.1.

Add an explicit statement of the new, citable scientific knowledge the validation framework yields and what is currently not achievable, so the beyond-the-state-of-the-art claim rests on a demonstrable advance rather than process rigour alone.

Evidence that the modelling/EO training capacity at ELTE is secured (imminent associated-partner and co-supervision confirmations) and describe the host-side continuity safeguard for the central training strand if the associated-partner arrangement changes.

Introduce conditional, method-anchored expected-effect ranges (detection lead-time, water-productivity improvement envelopes the design is powered to show) so the project's own magnitude is quantified as a defensible expectation, not only literature context.
Provide a month-by-month effort-loading view at the WP1/WP3/WP4 overlap and show how partner in-kind support offloads the fellow, to demonstrate the single-researcher concurrency is feasible.
Reassign WP3 scientific leadership to the fellow/beneficiary with the farmer site as a hosting environment, and cite the T3.1 access agreement and contingency ladder as the mitigating controls.
Foreground concrete modelling/EO artefacts (existing DrR functionality, datasets, tool outputs) to evidence hands-on capability while keeping the honest competence-gap framing.
Anchor the employability breadth in one or two concrete post-fellowship trajectories and cite the specific career KPI used to measure the career outcome.
Add a small set of measurable dissemination/uptake indicators (audiences reached, farmer participants, MVP evaluation users) tied to named channels, proportionate to a single-researcher action.

Quantify the near-term reachable segment (e.g. processing-tomato area in the target countries) alongside the EU-domain figure so the scale claim is graduated from what the action touches to the wider potential.
Renumber the work packages consecutively or add a one-line note that the former WP2 was merged into WP1, so the numbering gap is not read as an omission.

Reinforce participating-organisation capacity by evidencing the operational competence that substitutes for a research track record and confirming that PIC registration and host Part A legal-status verification are in hand before submission.
